ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=-x+3$ intersects the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{2}{x}$ $(x>0)$ at points A and B. What are the coordinates of points A and B?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution}: From the given problem, we have \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} y=-x+3 \\ y=\frac{2}{x} \end{array} \right. \] Therefore, $-x+3=\frac{2}{x}$, solving this gives $x_1=1$, $x_2=2$, $y_1=2$, $y_2=1$; therefore, the points are \boxed{A(1, 2)}, \boxed{B(2, 1)}.
